evidence.claim: The Boom or Bust Byway follows Highway 2 through Caddo, Bossier, Webster and Claiborne parishes, between the Texas border area and Lake Claiborne.
evidence.quote: The Boom or Bust Byway follows Highway 2 and is defined by the Louisiana/Texas border and Hwy. 3049 on the west and Lake Claiborne on the east. The Byway is comprised of four parishes: Caddo, Bossier, Webster, and Claiborne.

evidence.claim: At the western end, the two-lane road bends past the tip of Caddo Lake.
evidence.quote: LA 2 proceeds east as an undivided two-lane highway through the community of Trees then curves to the northeast and back to the east around the tip of Caddo Lake

evidence.claim: Boom or Bust Byway highlights farm crops, roadside trees and disused oilfield equipment.
evidence.quote: Travelers can relax in the serene scenery which includes lush, plentiful farm crops, tons of berries, wild flowers, and a never-ending background of trees

evidence.claim: farm crops
evidence.quote: lush, plentiful farm crops

evidence.claim: disused oilfield equipment.
evidence.quote: graveyards of longstanding oil field equipment that died when the oil industry went bust

evidence.claim: National Scenic Byway designation followed in 2021.
evidence.quote: The Bayou Teche Byway and Boom or Bust Byway were both designated National Scenic Byways.
February 19, 2021

evidence.claim: The route explores the changing fortunes of oil and gas, lumber, transportation, farming and entertainment.
evidence.quote: The 137-mile Boom or Bust Byway tells of the dramatic ups and downs in the oil and gas, lumber, transportation, farming and entertainment businesses over the decades.

evidence.claim: Highway 2 took its number in Louisiana’s 1955 highway renumbering.
evidence.quote: LA 2 was created with the 1955 Louisiana Highway renumbering

evidence.claim: It originally entered Homer’s courthouse square, but a northern bypass opened in 1964.
evidence.quote: The current alignment bypassing Homer to the north was opened in 1964

evidence.claim: It originally entered Homer’s courthouse square
evidence.quote: LA 2 originally followed LA 3062 into downtown Homer.  Upon reaching the intersection with US 79 and LA 9 at the courthouse square

evidence.claim: In the early 1970s, another change sent the road through Shongaloo before turning toward Leton.
evidence.quote: LA 2 assumed its current alignment between Sykes Ferry and Leton in the early 1970s following what was previously LA 2 Alt. to Shongaloo and co-signed with LA 159 to Leton.

evidence.claim: Shongaloo
evidence.quote: It then curves back to the northeast toward Shongaloo

evidence.claim: Parts of older alignments survive as local roads, including Old Homer Road near Blackburn and Old Lisbon Road at LA 806.
evidence.quote: Remnants of the original route exist today as short sections of local roads such as Old Homer Road near Blackburn, Old Lisbon Road at LA 806

evidence.claim: Travel east from the Caddo Lake area through Vivian and Hosston, then cross the Red River into Bossier Parish.
evidence.quote: 3.0 miles (4.8 km) outside of Hosston, LA 2 crosses a bridge over the Red River and into Bossier Parish.

evidence.claim: through Vivian and Hosston
evidence.quote: LA 2 turns north, running concurrent with LA 1 along the Kansas City Southern Railway (KCS) tracks into Vivian.

evidence.claim: through Vivian and Hosston
evidence.quote: After 4.8 miles (7.7 km), LA 2 enters Hosston

evidence.claim: Plain Dealing, Sarepta and Shongaloo follow before the road turns toward Homer.
evidence.quote: In Webster Parish, LA 2 enters Sarepta

evidence.claim: Plain Dealing, Sarepta and Shongaloo follow before the road turns toward Homer.
evidence.quote: In Bossier Parish, LA 2 intersects LA 537 and continues east for another 3.7 miles (6.0 km) into Plain Dealing.

evidence.claim: At Plain Dealing, the road briefly widens to four lanes before narrowing again as it leaves town with LA 157.
evidence.quote: Proceeding east from this intersection, LA 2 widens to an undivided four-lane highway.

evidence.claim: At Plain Dealing, the road briefly widens to four lanes before narrowing again as it leaves town with LA 157.
evidence.quote: LA 157 joins LA 2 eastward out of Plain Dealing, narrowing again to two lanes

evidence.claim: Germantown Colony lies on a separate excursion north of Minden.
evidence.quote: about 7 miles (11 km) north of Minden

evidence.claim: Beyond Homer, Highway 2 passes the northern end of Lake Claiborne.
evidence.quote: LA 2 continues due east past the northern end of Lake Claiborne

evidence.claim: Flooded cypress forest is part of Caddo Lake’s wetland landscape on the Texas–Louisiana border.
evidence.quote: The lake and bayou comprise an internationally protected wetland under the Ramsar Convention and includes one of the largest flooded cypress forests in the United States.

evidence.claim: on the Texas–Louisiana border.
evidence.quote: on the border between Texas and Louisiana

evidence.claim: Before oil, riverboat ports served the lake. Removal of logjams lowered its water level by more than ten feet, reducing navigability and undermining the East Texas ports.
evidence.quote: the lake changed shape and eventually its water level dropped by more than 10 feet (3.0 m). This dramatically reduced navigability by riverboat and ended the success of the East Texas ports.

evidence.claim: Before oil, riverboat ports served the lake.
evidence.quote: had thriving riverboat ports on the lake.

evidence.claim: Removal of logjams lowered its water level
evidence.quote: Gradually as the log jams were removed in the lake and on the Red River

evidence.claim: In 1911, Gulf Refining Company erected the Ferry Lake No. 1 oil platform here.
evidence.quote: The world's first over-water oil platform was completed in Caddo Lake in 1911.  The Ferry Lake No. 1 was erected by Gulf Refining Company.

evidence.claim: Derricks spread across the lake, damaging its ecosystem, before the industry moved to richer fields in Texas.
evidence.quote: Oil derricks were erected throughout the lake, further damaging the fragile ecosystem. The oil industry left Caddo for richer fields at Kilgore and other locations in Texas.

evidence.claim: Protection expanded in 1993 when Caddo Lake became a Ramsar wetland, part of an international effort to protect important wetlands.
evidence.quote: in October 1993 Caddo Lake became one of thirteen areas in the United States protected by the Ramsar Convention.  This is an international effort to protect important wetlands for sustainability.

evidence.claim: Dovetailed corners join the hewn logs of Countess Leon’s home and the kitchen-dining hall at Germantown.
evidence.quote: Countess Leon's home and the kitchen-dining hall, both built of hewn logs with dovetailing at their corners.

evidence.claim: Elisa Leon led the founding of the German religious community in 1836.
evidence.quote: It was founded in 1836 by Germans

evidence.claim: Elisa Leon led the founding
evidence.quote: Its founding was led by Elisa Leon

evidence.claim: Its community of about thirty-five people held property in common and followed religious principles.
evidence.quote: Though the colony was not very large, only about thirty-five people, it worked together and prospered.

evidence.claim: held property in common and followed religious principles.
evidence.quote: In the colony, all property was owned in common and observance of religious principles was required.

evidence.claim: Civil War privation and the colony’s pacifism contributed to the hardships that preceded its end as a commune in 1871.
evidence.quote: Its pacificism and general privation contributed to hardship during the American Civil War which contributed to its ending.

evidence.claim: its end as a commune in 1871.
evidence.quote: it lasted as a commune until 1871.

evidence.claim: The two surviving buildings have replacement windows, and none of their porches are original.
evidence.quote: Many windows have been replaced, and none of the porches are original.

evidence.claim: Most of the colony’s houses, barns, stores and shops have disappeared. The kitchen-dining hall retains a stone cellar beneath its log construction.
evidence.quote: The kitchen-dining hall has a dry wall stone cellar

evidence.claim: Most of the colony’s houses, barns, stores and shops have disappeared.
evidence.quote: Germantown once had numerous houses, barns, stores, and shops, as well as a kitchen-dining hall and a "bachelor's hall".  The historic buildings are mostly gone

evidence.claim: Homer’s 1860 brick courthouse predates the oil boom that brought guests to the Claiborne Hotel across the square.
evidence.quote: The building, completed in 1860

evidence.claim: brick courthouse
evidence.quote: The present-day brick courthouse, built in the Greek Revival style of architecture

evidence.claim: the oil boom that brought guests to the Claiborne Hotel across the square.
evidence.quote: The boom continued through the 1930s and brought many guests to the Hotel Claiborne

evidence.claim: across the square.
evidence.quote: located across the historic town square from the Claiborne Parish Courthouse.

evidence.claim: Oil discoveries at Homer and Haynesville in 1921 began a boom that continued through the 1930s.
evidence.quote: In 1921, oil was discovered in Homer; another strike followed that same year in Haynesville in northern Claiborne Parish near the Arkansas state line. The boom continued through the 1930s

evidence.claim: The former hotel houses the Herbert S. Ford Memorial Museum.
evidence.quote: The Herbert S. Ford Memorial Museum is a museum of local history and culture housed in the former Claiborne Hotel

evidence.claim: Its exhibits place a compressed cotton bale beside a replica oilfield laborer.
evidence.quote: "Black Gold", a replica of an oilfield roughneck, a general laborer who loads and unloads cargo from crane baskets and keeps the drilling equipment clean, is located next to the cotton exhibit.

evidence.claim: a compressed cotton bale
evidence.quote: The museum claims to hold the oldest compressed bale of cotton in existence in the United States.

evidence.claim: A recording follows a Mississippi farm family’s move to Claiborne Parish for opportunities in oil and gas.
evidence.quote: A recording explains how a farm family growing primarily cotton and corn faced economic travail in Mississippi but relocated to Claiborne Parish to benefit from opportunities in the oil and natural gas boom.

evidence.claim: The museum has housed Ford’s collection in the former hotel since 1982; the collection itself began in 1924 and previously occupied several locations.
evidence.quote: the museum has housed the collection of Homer businessman Herbert Ford (1889-1960) since 1982. Prior to that, the collection first started in 1924 had been in a variety of locations.
